links.outcome: Readability (FKGL, FKRE, SMOG) of LLM ADHD educational responses versus recommended grade 6-8 level
links.effect: All three models exhibited high reading levels (FKGL > 12, FKRE < 40, SMOG > 12), exceeding recommended public-health readability standards of about Grade 6-8.
links.quote: However, all models exhibited high reading levels (FKGL > 12, FKRE < 40, SMOG > 12), exceeding recommended public-health readability standards for general audiences, which are typically around Grade 6-8.

links.outcome: Comprehensibility of LLM-generated educational content for non-specialist educators
links.effect: All models produced text with FKGL > 12, FKRE < 40, SMOG > 12, above recommended Grade 6-8 levels, restricting accessibility for non-specialist educators.
links.quote: However, all models exhibited high reading levels (FKGL > 12, FKRE < 40, SMOG > 12), exceeding recommended public-health readability standards for general audiences, which are typically around Grade 6-8.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation benchmarking the accuracy, stability, and readability of three LLMs (ChatGPT 5, DeepSeek V3, Grok 4) in generating educational content about ADHD.
